summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived biography of Empress Dowager Huang, an empress dowager of the Min state during the Chinese Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period. Her personal name is unknown, and she is called Empress Dowager Longqi after her son's era name. She was the primary concubine of Wang Shenzhi (Prince Zhongyi), regarded as the founder of Min, and the mother of Wang Yanjun, the first Min ruler to claim the title of emperor.
one_line: Empress Dowager Huang, primary concubine of Min founder Wang Shenzhi and mother of Emperor Huizong Wang Yanjun, of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period.
key_facts: Empress Dowager Huang's personal name is unknown.
Empress Dowager Huang is written as 黃太后 in Chinese.
Empress Dowager Huang is referred to semi-formally as Empress Dowager Longqi (龍啟太后).
The name Longqi comes from the era name of her son Wang Yanjun.
Empress Dowager Huang was an empress dowager of the Chinese Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period state Min.
Wang Shenzhi, also known as Prince Zhongyi, was commonly regarded as the founder of the Min state.
Empress Dowager Huang was the primary concubine of Wang Shenzhi.
Empress Dowager Huang was the mother of Wang Yanjun.
Wang Yanjun was also known as Wang Lin and as Emperor Huizong.
Wang Yanjun was the first Min ruler to claim the title of emperor.
